title: Architecting for non-deterministic components
title_ko: 비결정적 구성 요소를 위한 아키텍처 설계
summary_ko: 스스로 판단하고 행동하는 AI 구성 요소를 시스템에 안전하게 통합하기 위한 아키텍처 원칙을 다룹니다.
abstract: Our systems used to behave the same way every time. Now we give them judgment and agency, so they decide and act on their own, and the same inputs can produce different outcomes. Designing reliable architectures around that non-determinism comes down to three questions: where to enforce determinism around the model, when to verify behavior through automated evaluation and reasoning versus human judgment, and how to adapt the patterns (event flows, orchestration, automation) for components that don’t behave predictably. This session presents the design patterns for building systems that decide and act, while preserving the reliability your architecture depends on.

title: Find failure modes faster: AI-powered resilience assessments
title_ko: 더 빠르게 장애 모드 찾기: AI 기반 복원력 평가
summary_ko: AWS Resilience Hub의 생성형 AI 평가 엔진으로 애플리케이션의 장애 모드를 빠르게 찾아내는 실습입니다.
abstract: Manual resilience reviews are slow, inconsistent, and routinely miss failure modes that don't surface until an incident occurs. In this workshop, you'll use the generative AI-driven assessment engine in AWS Resilience Hub to automatically discover dependencies across AWS services, internal endpoints, and third-party systems. You'll evaluate workloads against the Well-Architected Framework and your own defined resilience policies including availability SLOs, RTO, and RPO targets, then receive prioritized, actionable recommendations tied to business impact. Working with a reference architecture, you'll build a complete end-to-end assessment and leave with a repeatable framework you can run against any workload as your architecture evolves. Bring your laptop to participate.

title: Queue-based decoupling trade-offs for event-driven workloads
title_ko: 이벤트 기반 워크로드를 위한 큐 기반 디커플링의 트레이드오프
summary_ko: 정확히 한 번 처리 등 상충하는 요구가 있는 시나리오를 통해 큐 기반 디커플링의 장단점을 분석합니다.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Builders' Session 1
abstract: Every decoupling pattern makes trade-offs, and the right one depends on your workload's constraints. In this session, you work through scenarios with competing demands: exactly-once processing, tenant isolation, back pressure, and ordering. Using SQS and Lambda, you configure queue types and concurrency controls, tune batching behavior, and observe how your consumer scales under each configuration. Each scenario forces a trade-off between throughput, ordering, isolation, and cost. You leave knowing which trade-offs to accept for your workload and why. Bring your laptop to participate.

title: Break it to prove It: Fault-isolated architecture built to recover
title_ko: 깨뜨려서 증명하라: 복구를 위해 설계된 장애 격리 아키텍처
summary_ko: 단일 리전과 멀티 리전 복원력 패턴을 구현하고 장애를 주입해 복구 능력을 검증하는 워크숍입니다.
abstract: Your recovery plan is only as good as the architecture backing it. This workshop presents single-Region and multi-Region resilience patterns built along fault isolation boundaries, where failure scope dictates which recovery mechanism to engage. Using Amazon Application Recovery Controller (ARC), you architect for discrete blast radii, then validate each boundary through fault injection with AWS Fault Injection Service. Observability surfaces the failure, alarms classify scope, and automated recovery executes without intervention. The result: proof that your architecture recovers the way you designed it to. Bring your laptop to participate.

title: Well-Architected in your AI coding agent: Find gaps before you commit
title_ko: AI 코딩 에이전트에 Well-Architected 적용: 커밋 전에 격차 찾기
summary_ko: 하루에도 수십 번 아키텍처 결정을 내리는 AI 코딩 에이전트에 Well-Architected 점검을 통합하는 방법을 다룹니다.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Builders' Session 2
abstract: Architecture reviews happen at milestones: a design review here, an operational readiness check there. But AI coding agents make architectural decisions dozens of times a day, and governance that runs at milestone pace can't keep up. In this session, you will configure open-source Well-Architected skills in your coding agent, run a full Well-Architected review and catch resilience, security, and operational gaps in minutes. Then author a custom skill that encodes your team's standards and trade-offs. You leave with a review loop that runs every commit. Bring your laptop to participate.

title: When agents disagree: Resolving competing goals in cloud operations
title_ko: 에이전트 의견이 엇갈릴 때: 클라우드 운영의 상충 목표 해결
summary_ko: Well-Architected 원칙별 에이전트들의 상충 목표를 합의 계층으로 조정하는 클라우드 운영 패턴을 소개합니다.
abstract: When two agents manage the same workload, each optimizing a different objective, conflicting actions are the default, not the exception. A consensus layer changes the pattern: pillar-aligned agents carry workload goals and live signals as context, reason toward agreement, and produce a single decision playbook before any action executes. In this session, you build one pillar agent from scratch, configure its context layer, connect it to the consensus flow, and watch shared context resolve a live disagreement without rules or priority overrides. Bring your laptop to participate.

title: Multi-agent AI: Orchestration and choreography, compared
title_ko: 멀티 에이전트 AI: 오케스트레이션과 코레오그래피 비교
summary_ko: 중앙 오케스트레이터와 분산 코레오그래피 중 다음 행동을 누가 결정할지에 따른 멀티 에이전트 설계 방식을 비교합니다.
abstract: Every multi-agent AI system needs a coordination layer. The hard question is who decides what happens next: a central orchestrator or the agents themselves. In this session, you deploy the same five-agent travel booking pipeline through both orchestration (Step Functions) and choreography (EventBridge). Run identical load tests, inject the same failures, and add a sixth agent to each. Measure blast radius, extensibility cost, and debugging speed to see where the two approaches diverge. Leave knowing when to orchestrate, when to choreograph, and how to combine both in one architecture. Bring your laptop to participate.

title: Red, green, re-architect: Test-driven infrastructure
title_ko: 레드, 그린, 리아키텍트: 테스트 주도 인프라
summary_ko: 아키텍처를 자연어로 기술하고 Kiro의 스펙 기반 개발로 테스트 주도 방식의 인프라를 구축합니다.
abstract: AI can write your infrastructure in seconds — but did it build what you asked for? In this workshop, you'll apply test-driven development to AI-generated infrastructure. Describe your architecture in plain English, then use Kiro's spec-driven development to decompose it into discrete, testable behaviors. Kiro iterates through each one: writing a failing CDK assertion that encodes it (red), generating minimal infrastructure to pass it (green), then advancing to the next. Once green, refactor toward production readiness using cdk-nag rule packs to enforce Well-Architected practices. Leave with meaningful test coverage and a repeatable pattern for raising your organization's infrastructure coding standards. Bring your laptop to participate.

title: Architect resilient agentic systems: Patterns beyond the happy path
title_ko: 복원력 있는 에이전틱 시스템 설계: 정상 경로를 넘어선 패턴
summary_ko: 추론 도중 타임아웃 등 AI 에이전트의 다양한 장애 상황에 대응하는 복원력 있는 설계 패턴을 다룹니다.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Builders' Session 1
abstract: Every agentic system works on the happy path. The real test is what happens when your AI agent times out mid-reasoning, returns a malformed action, or cascades a single failure across an entire chain. In this session, you implement four resilience patterns built for non-deterministic agents: circuit breakers that trip on semantic failure, fallback hierarchies from AI to rules to human, bulkhead isolation between agents, and timeout budgets for chain-of-thought latency. Leave with a decision framework mapping failure modes to pattern combinations you can implement immediately. Bring your laptop to participate.

title: Where embeddings live: Designing production retrieval on AWS
title_ko: 임베딩은 어디에 두어야 하나: AWS에서 프로덕션 검색 설계
summary_ko: 동일한 검색 패턴을 Amazon OpenSearch 등 세 가지 엔진에 구현해 보며 임베딩 저장소 선택 기준을 비교합니다.
abstract: Where should vector embeddings live? In your operational database, a dedicated vector store, or across several? In this session you evaluate the trade-offs across latency, data freshness, cost, and retrieval quality. You implement the same retrieval pattern across three engines: Amazon OpenSearch Service for combined lexical and vector search, Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL with pgvector for SQL-native filtered retrieval, and Amazon S3 Vectors for cost-optimized scale. You learn the workload patterns these engines handle best, so you can tell where a single store is enough and where a hybrid architecture pays off. You leave able to answer where your embeddings should live, backed by patterns you built yourself. Bring your laptop to participate.

title: From system thinking to outcome thinking: The AI-native architect
title_ko: 시스템 사고에서 성과 사고로: AI 네이티브 아키텍트
summary_ko: AI가 아키텍트의 구축 대상뿐 아니라 사고방식과 역할까지 어떻게 바꾸고 있는지 살펴봅니다.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Blue Theater
abstract: The architect role is changing faster than at any point since the cloud itself emerged. AI is reshaping not just what architects build, but how they think, where they spend their time, and what organizations expect. We share observations from leading a global transformation of thousands of AWS Solutions Architects into AI-native practitioners: what shifted in daily practice, what surprised us, and what broke. We explore how outcome-oriented thinking replaces system-oriented thinking, and why the line between building and advising is dissolving. You leave with a practical mental model for how the architecture role delivers value in an AI-native world.

title: Fault-tolerant AI agents: Choosing the right recovery pattern
title_ko: 내결함성 AI 에이전트: 올바른 복구 패턴 선택하기
summary_ko: 상태가 누적되는 에이전트에서 무분별한 재시도의 위험을 짚고 상황에 맞는 복구 패턴을 선택하는 방법을 다룹니다.
abstract: When an AI agent crashes at step 20 of 30, you can't just start over. Once state accumulates, an unexamined retry becomes dangerous. Most teams default to the wrong recovery strategy because they apply stateless retry thinking to stateful workflows. In this session, we compare three approaches: replay-based recovery with idempotent tool execution, checkpoint-and-resume with human-in-the-loop pause/resume, and event-driven compensation across trust boundaries. We'll whiteboard each pattern, map it to real failure scenarios, and build a decision framework based on your agent's state model and fault domain.

title: Architecting for resilience and data residency
title_ko: 복원력과 데이터 레지던시를 위한 아키텍처 설계
summary_ko: 복원력 확보와 데이터 레지던시 요구 사항을 동시에 충족하는 아키텍처 패턴을 살펴봅니다.
abstract: Your data can't leave the jurisdiction, but your workload still has to survive a Region degradation. This chalk talk explores architecture patterns that address both resilience and data residency together. We break the challenge into practical layers: where data lives, how workloads recover, what isolation looks like, and how to maintain business continuity across geographic boundaries. We map each layer to AWS capabilities including Dedicated Local Zones, Outposts, and policy controls, then work through real scenarios together. Bring your architecture challenges and we will whiteboard design patterns and tradeoffs with you.

title: Patterns for embedding FinOps into cloud architectural decisions
title_ko: 클라우드 아키텍처 의사결정에 FinOps를 내재화하는 패턴
summary_ko: 배포 전 단계에서 비용을 최적화하도록 FinOps를 설계 단계로 앞당기는 방법을 시연합니다.
abstract: Every architectural decision carries a cost implication, yet cost is typically discovered in monthly bills rather than design reviews. In this code talk, we demonstrate how to shift FinOps left, optimising before you deploy rather than reacting after. Through two personas, a FinOps engineer and a builder, you will see live how to embed cost governance into infrastructure-as-code, tackle real architectural trade-offs then show how AI coding assistants accelerate this at scale. You will leave with deployable CloudFormation examples and a decision framework for choosing the right cost governance level for your organisation.

title: Cell-based architecture: Designing blast-radius boundaries
title_ko: 셀 기반 아키텍처: 피해 반경 경계 설계하기
summary_ko: 고객, 지역, 워크로드 등 기준에 따라 셀 경계를 정해 장애 피해 반경을 제한하는 셀 기반 아키텍처를 다룹니다.
abstract: Cell-based architecture limits the blast radius of failures by partitioning systems into independent, isolated units. But deciding cell boundaries — by customer, geography, or workload — involves trade-offs between operational complexity and fault isolation. This session reveals the decision framework for cell sizing, routing, and cross-cell coordination. You'll learn when cells outperform active-active patterns, how to implement cell-aware deployments, and the true operational cost of cell management. Walk away with a reusable pattern for systems, where failures stay contained, impact reduced, and availability increased.

title: Multi-Region hedging: Where it works and where it breaks
title_ko: 멀티 리전 헤징: 효과가 있는 곳과 무너지는 곳
summary_ko: 멀티 리전 헤징 기법이 효과적인 상황과 한계에 부딪히는 상황을 분석합니다.
abstract: Failover recovers after impairment; hedging survives it. This chalk talk examines where multi-Region hedging holds and where it breaks. We trace hedging across the stack: racing requests through Route 53 ARC and Elastic Load Balancing, containing blast radius with cell-based routing, and confronting the write path, where Aurora Global Database's asynchronous replication surfaces a consistency-versus-continuity trade-off that routing alone cannot resolve. Bring your availability-critical workload; we'll map its hedgeable read and routing paths against those that force an explicit consistency decision.

title: Resilience patterns for the disconnected edge with Amazon Leo
title_ko: Amazon Leo로 구현하는 단절된 엣지를 위한 복원력 패턴
summary_ko: Amazon Leo 위성 연결 환경에서 라우팅, 전송 중 데이터 처리 등 단절된 엣지를 위한 복원력 설계 트레이드오프를 다룹니다.
abstract: Every resilient system eventually has to answer one question: what happens when the network you depend on isn’t there? In this session we discuss Amazon Leo, a low earth orbit satellite connectivity service, as a forcing function to explore patterns for architecting across unreliable, high-latency, and intermittently connected links. We’ll walk through the trade-offs behind routing, data-in-transit security, and where to place compute when bandwidth is scarce and connectivity is a variable. We’ll ground the discussion in hybrid resiliency and edge data collection for AI/ML, but the takeaway is portable to any architecture spanning boundaries you don’t fully control.

title: Deterministic meets probabilistic: Patterns for reliable AI integration
title_ko: 결정론과 확률론의 만남: 신뢰할 수 있는 AI 통합 패턴
summary_ko: 확률적인 AI 출력과 결정론적 시스템의 경계를 안정적으로 연결하는 통합 패턴을 소개합니다.
abstract: Production systems demand determinism. AI outputs are probabilistic. The boundary between these two worlds is where this must be resolved. This chalk talk will whiteboard the contracts and integration patterns that hold that boundary: typed interfaces treating model output as untrusted input, propose/commit separation so AI never performs its own side effects, asymmetric verification, bounded generate-verify-repair loops, and compensating actions in place of rollback. We'll work through typical anti-patterns that quietly reach production, where to place the contract in your architecture to avoid these, and the reliability arithmetic that these patterns enable.

title: Ambient accessibility: Architecting real-time ASL on a Wearable
title_ko: 앰비언트 접근성: 웨어러블에서 실시간 수어(ASL) 아키텍처 설계
summary_ko: 1초 이내 응답 제약 아래 웨어러블 기기에서 실시간 미국 수어 번역을 구현한 아키텍처 트레이드오프를 다룹니다.
abstract: What if a DHH person could wear a device and get sign language translation of every conversation around them in under a second? We architect a pipeline that ingests Amazon Bee's ambient audio, transcribes it, transforms English to ASL grammar, generates avatar animations, and streams signed video back. That one-second constraint drives every architectural tradeoff, from whether translation stages run on-device for speed or in the cloud for accuracy, to whether we sign full sentences or start mid-utterance with partial context. We explore the edge-cloud splits and pipeline staging that make sub-second delivery feasible.

title: Serverless at 1M RPS: Lambda, DynamoDB & SQS Scaling Lessons
title_ko: 초당 100만 요청의 서버리스: Lambda, DynamoDB, SQS 확장 교훈
summary_ko: 파티션을 고려한 DynamoDB 설계 등 초당 100만 요청 규모로 서버리스를 확장하며 얻은 교훈을 공유합니다.
abstract: We push Lambda, DynamoDB, and SQS to one million requests per second and share what breaks. Learn partition-aware DynamoDB design for extreme write throughput, Lambda concurrency shaping to prevent downstream crush, SQS as a backpressure buffer with adaptive batching, and retry amplification math that turns a blip into a cascade. We present real numbers: cold start budgets at scale, the exact crossover point where serverless cost exceeds containers, and the operational trade-offs at each threshold.

title: Serverless at 1M RPS: Lambda, DynamoDB & SQS Scaling Lessons
title_ko: 초당 100만 요청의 서버리스: Lambda, DynamoDB, SQS 확장 교훈

title: When one tenant spikes 100x, your architecture decides who pays
title_ko: 한 테넌트가 100배 급증할 때, 누가 대가를 치를지는 아키텍처가 결정한다
summary_ko: 특정 테넌트의 트래픽 급증이 다른 테넌트로 번지지 않도록 피해 반경을 격리하는 멀티테넌트 아키텍처를 다룹니다.
abstract: One tenant spikes 100x. The architecture either isolates the blast radius or turns it into every tenant's outage. Multi-tenant platforms face four decisions at this boundary. Where to place isolation so one workload cannot starve another. How fan-out creates backpressure that propagates upstream. When fair queuing replaces custom throttling code. What qualifies as real-time versus safely queueable. In this chalk talk you decide where your isolation boundaries belong and what trade-offs each placement creates. Bring your own scaling problem. We draw the architecture together.

title: Your system made a decision. you cannot explain it.
title_ko: 시스템이 내린 결정을 설명할 수 없다면
summary_ko: AI와 사람의 결정이 함께 기록되는 시스템에서 의사결정을 추적하고 설명 가능하게 만드는 설계 방법을 다룹니다.
abstract: Your system makes a decision. A human makes a decision. Both write to the same log in the same format. Three months later you need to know which was which. You cannot tell. This is not a logging problem. It is a runtime architecture problem. If decision origin is not captured at the boundary when the decision happens, no system can recover it after. Whether you need this for compliance, debugging, or customer trust, the architectural fix is identical. In this chalk talk you will decide: what to capture at the decision boundary, how much context to store, and when reproducibility justifies the cost.

title: Stop fixing, start preventing with Well-Architected Agent
title_ko: Well-Architected Agent로 고치지 말고 예방하라
summary_ko: AWS Well-Architected Agent로 아키텍처 문제를 사후 수정하는 대신 사전에 예방하는 방법을 소개합니다.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | White Theater
abstract: Reactive incident response grows more expensive as environments scale. AWS Well-Architected Agent shifts resilience and security from periodic review to continuous, automated assessment. Its agentic reasoning identifies single points of failure, recovery gaps, and vulnerabilities across 100+ services, ranking findings by workload criticality and business goals. Crucially, each recommendation includes cross-pillar trade-off analysis - showing cost and performance implications — so you improve resilience and security without unintended consequences elsewhere. Walk away able to catch risks before they become incidents.

title: The coordination decision: when to orchestrate and when to let go
title_ko: 조율의 결정: 언제 오케스트레이션하고 언제 맡길 것인가
summary_ko: 오케스트레이션과 자율 조율 방식이 대규모에서 각각 실패하는 이유를 살펴보고 적절한 선택 기준을 제시합니다.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Red Theater
abstract: Distributed workflows need coordination, and most teams pick one approach everywhere: a central orchestrator, or independent services reacting to events. Both fail at scale: orchestration bottlenecks every team's releases, and choreography lets flows stall silently because no component owns the outcome. This session teaches a per-flow method: does any component need to own the flow end-to-end, including completion, failure compensation, and ordering? Using a logistics platform running both patterns on AWS Step Functions and Amazon EventBridge, see the real costs of each, and where orchestration and events hand off.

title: Pitfalls of SaaS: Return of the agent
title_ko: SaaS의 함정: 에이전트의 귀환
summary_ko: 기존 SaaS의 함정을 증폭시키고 새로운 문제를 더하는 AI 에이전트 도입 시 주의할 점을 다룹니다.
abstract: Every SaaS architect has hit the classics: noisy neighbors saturating infrastructure, compounding costs eating margins, deployment models chosen too early. Agents amplify all of them — and add surprises. One agent generates more API calls in a minute than a human makes in a week. Shared memory leaks context across tenants in ways no IAM policy catches. Autonomous tool calls cascade across services with no human in the loop. Revisit classic SaaS pitfalls through an agentic lens: familiar problems in new costumes, genuinely new failure modes, and what to change before you find out the hard way.

title: SaaS Agents Anywhere: building distributed agentic deployments
title_ko: 어디서나 SaaS 에이전트: 분산 에이전틱 배포 구축
summary_ko: 데이터 레지던시와 비용 가시성 요구에 대응해 SaaS 에이전트를 분산 배포하는 아키텍처를 다룹니다.
abstract: SaaS vendors deploy agents across a spectrum: fully provider-hosted, fully tenant-controlled, and hybrid models in between. Once customers have data residency or cost-visibility requirements, deployment topology determines the operational pattern. In this workshop, build a distributed agentic deployment on AWS spanning your accounts and a tenant's, then exercise the three concerns that surface everywhere on the spectrum: lifecycle management of agents you can't directly see, observability across account boundaries, and reliability when the agent runs somewhere you don't operate. Leave with a working reference deployment you can adapt to your own tenancy model.

title: Unexpected resilience: Lessons from a thousand incidents
title_ko: 예상치 못한 복원력: 천 건의 장애에서 얻은 교훈
summary_ko: 런북으로 예측할 수 없었던 수많은 장애 사례에서 얻은 복원력에 관한 교훈을 공유합니다.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Ballroom F | Content Hub | Purple Theater
abstract: After years of investigating incidents - both within AWS and across customer industries - some resilience lessons stand out. Not the obvious ones, but surprises no runbook could anticipate. We share the strangest, most counterintuitive findings from years of troubleshooting under pressure: failure modes nobody planned for, fixes that made things worse, and patterns that only emerge after enough failures. This isn't a best-practices talk - it's a field guide to building resilience from the unexpected. You'll leave with a sharper eye for hidden risks in your infrastructure - and fresh leads on things you didn't know were there.

title: Inverting the medallion: Serving reads without hitting Gold
title_ko: 메달리온 뒤집기: Gold 계층을 거치지 않고 읽기 제공하기
summary_ko: 헬스 데이터나 원장 같은 규제 대상 기록 시스템에서 Gold 계층 없이 읽기를 제공하는 데이터 아키텍처를 다룹니다.
abstract: Most teams default to Gold as the serving layer. For regulated systems-of-record like health data stores, ledgers, compliance archives, that's rarely the right choice. They're built for durability and interoperability, not production read traffic. The inverted pattern writes promote up the medallion, reads come from purpose-built Silver projections and Gold holds contractual semantics and never serves directly. In this chalk talk, work through change-data-capture synthesis without source support, write/read path splitting, and a routing gateway developers can't bypass. Bring your most painful regulated read path. Leave knowing when to invert, how to scope projections, and what your gateway must enforce.

title: Build Resilient AI Platforms with Oracle AI Database@AWS (sponsored by Oracle)
title_ko: Oracle AI Database@AWS로 복원력 있는 AI 플랫폼 구축 (Oracle 후원)
summary_ko: Oracle Maximum Availability Architecture로 Oracle AI Database@AWS 기반 AI 워크로드를 보호하는 방법을 배웁니다.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Builder Theater
abstract: AI applications demand continuous access to trusted, business-critical data. In this lightning session, learn how Oracle Maximum Availability Architecture helps protect AI workloads running on Oracle AI Database@AWS. Explore proven patterns for high availability, disaster recovery, data protection, and automated failover across AWS Availability Zones and Regions. See how capabilities such as Oracle Active Data Guard and integrated backup and recovery services help minimize downtime, reduce data loss, and keep AI applications operating through planned maintenance and unexpected disruptions. This presentation is brought to you by Oracle, an AWS Partner.

title: Route or escalate: Confidence boundaries in multi-domain AI agents
title_ko: 라우팅할 것인가, 에스컬레이션할 것인가: 멀티 도메인 AI 에이전트의 신뢰도 경계
summary_ko: 멀티 에이전트와 RAG 시스템에서 신뢰도에 따라 요청을 라우팅하거나 사람에게 에스컬레이션하는 설계 방법을 다룹니다.
abstract: Building a GenAI system that answers questions across technology domains is straightforward — until the model doesn't know the answer and doesn't say so. For builders designing multi-agent or RAG-based systems, this session presents the confidence-gated routing architecture: classifying every query into high-confidence retrieval, low-confidence escalation to a human specialist, or cross-domain composition. We cover why flat vector retrieval fails multi-domain queries, the trade-offs of graph-based knowledge ontology, and the evaluations framework measuring confidence calibration. Walk away with a routing pattern you can apply any time your AI system must self-report uncertainty rather than hallucinate with authority.

title_ko: 라우팅할 것인가, 에스컬레이션할 것인가: 멀티 도메인 AI 에이전트의 신뢰도 경계

title: Foundational architecture excellence: the operability trade-off
title_ko: 기초 아키텍처 우수성: 운영성과의 트레이드오프
summary_ko: 운영 현실을 무시한 아키텍처가 어떻게 운영 부채를 만드는지, 수많은 엔터프라이즈 사례를 바탕으로 설계 결정의 함정을 살펴봅니다.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Industry Theater
abstract: Elegant architectures that ignore operational reality become expensive liabilities. From hundreds of enterprise engagements, we expose the architectural decisions that silently create operational debt — decomposition without observability boundaries, blast-radius assumptions that fail under correlated load, and abstraction layers hiding the signals operators need. We unpack where good architecture and operable architecture diverge, which trade-offs are worth making early, and what questions your team should be asking before committing to a design. The best architecture is one you can actually run in production.

title: Architecting for five nines with multi-region: Capital One’s journey (sponsored by Capital One)
title_ko: 멀티 리전으로 파이브 나인 가용성 설계하기: Capital One의 여정 (후원: Capital One)
summary_ko: Capital One이 연간 5분 남짓의 다운타임 한도 안에서 리전 장애를 견디도록 멀티 리전 아키텍처를 발전시킨 과정을 소개합니다.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade South | Octavius 4 | Content Hub | Purple Theater
abstract: Five nines of availability leaves an annual downtime budget of just 5.2 minutes, meaning a single regional failover can consume your entire year. Traditional disaster recovery models simply don't scale to meet this standard. In this session, discover how Capital One evolved its multi-region architectures to sustain regional outages while supporting critical production workloads. We share lessons learned from building and operating active-active topologies, focusing on real-world data consistency models, fault isolation via cell-based architecture, and continuous fault-injection testing. Attendees will walk away with a field-tested matrix for architecting high-availability cloud workloads. This presentation is brought to you by Capital One, an AWS Partner.

title: Thousands of Databases, $250 a Month: Operating an Agentic Database Estate on AWS (sponsored by CockroachDB)
title_ko: 수천 개의 데이터베이스를 월 250달러로: AWS에서 에이전틱 데이터베이스 운영하기 (후원: CockroachDB)
summary_ko: 유휴 용량 낭비 없이 약 1,000개의 프로덕션급 데이터베이스를 저비용으로 운영하는 에이전틱 데이터베이스 관리 방식을 다룹니다.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Ballroom F | Content Hub | Purple Theater
abstract: What if ~1,000 production-grade databases cost $250/month? Most teams pay more to keep a few clusters idle, each sized for peak load, running at 85–95% unused capacity and provisioned ticket by ticket. That model is breaking. AI agents create databases faster than platform teams can provision, secure or retire them. One engineering group grew from 13 databases to 392 in four months. At 1,000, managing one cluster at a time stops working. This session shifts focus to the estate with 3 architectural changes on AWS: - Separate storage from compute, eliminating upfront capacity. - Run isolated virtual clusters on shared hosts without creating sprawl. - Use agentic operations to observe the estate and recommend actions your team approves. See live demos, a reference architecture and cost model behind the numbers. Bring your hardest questions about running stateful workloads at agent speed. This presentation is brought to you by CockroachDB, an AWS Partner.

title: Close the loop: From guardrail blocks into layered defense
title_ko: 루프 닫기: 가드레일 차단에서 계층형 방어로
summary_ko: 가드레일이 차단한 프롬프트를 신호로 수집해 상태 기반 탐지를 포함한 계층형 보안 집행 아키텍처를 직접 설계하고 배포합니다.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Builders' Session 1
abstract: Guardrails block malicious prompts. Every blocked attempt is a signal: proof of what your defenses caught and a clue toward what will be attempted next. Capture that signal instead of discarding it. In this session, you design and deploy a layered enforcement architecture that closes the loop. A stateful detection tier identifies repeated probing across sessions and propagates block decisions to the network edge. You evaluate signals from guardrail violations and apply policies to classify and block the threat. You leave with a deployed pattern applicable to any AI agent workload. Bring your laptop to participate.

title: Event storming: Find your service boundaries before production does
title_ko: 이벤트 스토밍: 프로덕션보다 먼저 서비스 경계 찾기
summary_ko: 분산 모놀리스를 피하기 위해 이벤트 스토밍 기법으로 올바른 서비스 경계를 함께 도출하는 실습형 세션입니다.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Builders' Session 1
abstract: Split a system in the wrong place and you get a distributed monolith: coupled services with network hops instead of function calls. This session tackles the problem most teams get wrong, where to draw the boundary, using Event Storming. Together we map a real domain, trace information flow between actors, and identify natural division points, deciding ownership, data locality, transaction scope, and deployment independence at each boundary. Every decision is evidence based, grounded in observed event flow rather than intuition. Then you go hands on, taking one boundary and deploying it as an independent service on AWS. Leave with a repeatable method for boundary definition plus working code you built yourself. Bring your laptop.

title: Event storming: Find your service boundaries before production does
title_ko: 이벤트 스토밍: 프로덕션보다 먼저 서비스 경계 찾기
summary_ko: 분산 모놀리스를 피하기 위해 이벤트 스토밍 기법으로 올바른 서비스 경계를 함께 도출하는 실습형 세션입니다.

title: Your regulator set your RTO. Not your architecture.
title_ko: RTO를 정하는 건 아키텍처가 아니라 규제 기관이다
summary_ko: 사전 승인된 장애 조치 리전 등 거버넌스 결정이 복구 시간을 좌우하는 이유와 규제 환경에서의 복원력 설계를 다룹니다.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | White Theater
abstract: Organizations with pre-approved failover regions recover in hours. Those without recover in weeks. Same impairment. Same services. One governance decision separates them, and it’s made years before the event. This session presents architectural patterns for multi-Region recovery under sovereignty constraints, drawn from real operational experience with regulated workloads under regional pressure. Three categories: decisions that set your resilience ceiling before any event, dependencies that create circular failure during recovery, and assets nobody backs up until they become the critical path. You leave with the decisions to evaluate before your next DR test.

title: Visualizing multi-tenant isolation: Catch your noisy neighbors
title_ko: 멀티 테넌트 격리 시각화: 시끄러운 이웃 잡아내기
summary_ko: 멀티 테넌트 플랫폼에서 테넌트 데이터 격리와 노이지 네이버 문제를 시각화하고 비용·성능 트레이드오프 속에서 해결하는 방법을 다룹니다.
abstract: Managing multi-tenant platforms forces trade-offs between cost, complexity, and performance. This session tackles two common challenges: tenant data isolation and the noisy-neighbor problem. Starting from a single-tenant architecture, you consolidate into a shared Amazon Aurora MySQL cluster, building isolation through Cognito-issued JWTs, Lambda-based dynamic policy generation, IAM authentication, and RDS Proxy connection pooling. Then you implement queuing tiers with Amazon SQS to manage load. Visualize real-time request flows, data isolation, and noisy-neighbor effects on your own dynamic architecture simulation and a central 16,000-LED display. Bring your laptop to participate.

title: Data mesh at scale: The automation layer, proven at Experian
title_ko: 대규모 데이터 메시: Experian에서 검증된 자동화 계층
summary_ko: 연합형 데이터 소유권에서 거버넌스를 프로세스가 아닌 플랫폼 자동화로 집행하는 방법을 Experian 사례로 살펴봅니다.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Red Theater
abstract: Federated data ownership is easy to draw and hard to enforce. Is governance enforced in process, or in the platform? Enforce it in the platform, and the hard part becomes the seam between central policy and self-serve provisioning most teams never build. On Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio we architect that seam: one project per data-domain for blast-radius isolation, contracts that block non-compliant publication, policy that cascades but only tightens, and a reconciler turning Git-committed JSON into infrastructure. Experian runs it across dozens of data domains in regulated financial services, cutting domain onboarding from months to self-serve.

title: Specs, not vibes: Strangling the monolith in the IDE
title_ko: 감이 아닌 스펙으로: IDE에서 모놀리스 교살하기
summary_ko: 슬라이드 없이 Kiro와 스펙 기반 개발로 IDE에서 스트랭글러 패턴을 활용한 모놀리스 분해를 라이브로 시연하는 코드 토크입니다.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Code Talk
abstract: Your architecture is full of pets: brittle EC2 instances run by manual runbooks, with no contract between decisions and infrastructure. In this code talk, we abandon slides and prove the Strangler pattern live in the IDE with Kiro and spec-driven development. We decompose a monolith into bounded contexts, generate CDK from the spec, and shift traffic from pets to serverless cattle, confronting the hard parts: where to cut the seam, running old and new together, keeping data consistent. Every architectural decision becomes a machine-verifiable contract you can apply to your own monolith.

title: Specs, not vibes: Strangling the monolith in the IDE
title_ko: 감이 아닌 스펙으로: IDE에서 모놀리스 교살하기
summary_ko: 슬라이드 없이 Kiro와 스펙 기반 개발로 IDE에서 스트랭글러 패턴을 활용한 모놀리스 분해를 라이브로 시연하는 코드 토크입니다.
abstract: Your architecture is full of pets: brittle EC2 instances run by manual runbooks, with no contract between decisions and infrastructure. In this code talk, we abandon slides and prove the Strangler pattern live in the IDE with Kiro and spec-driven development. We decompose a monolith into bounded contexts, generate CDK from the spec, and shift traffic from pets to serverless cattle, confronting the hard parts: where to cut the seam, running old and new together, keeping data consistent. Every architectural decision becomes a machine-verifiable contract you can apply to your own monolith.

title: Load-bearing coupling: Finding the coupling you can't cut
title_ko: 하중을 지탱하는 결합: 끊을 수 없는 결합 찾기
summary_ko: 실제 시스템을 화이트보드로 분석하며 이음새를 넣고 각 의존성이 경계를 넘을 때 드는 비용을 따져 봅니다.
abstract: Teams break up monoliths to move faster, then find the pieces still fail together. Some coupling is doing real structural work: invariants spanning writes, ordering guarantees, timing assumptions baked into callers. Cut it and you get a distributed monolith, the same dependency with new failure modes. In this session, we whiteboard real systems, insert seams, and price what each dependency costs to cross a boundary: consistency, backpressure, retry semantics. Apply a simple test: if a circuit breaker can't open here without breaking correctness, that coupling is load-bearing. Bring your hardest dependency; leave knowing which coupling to cut, which to keep, and why.

title: Twenty years of cloud architecture
title_ko: 클라우드 아키텍처 20년
summary_ko: 탄력성, IaC, 최종 일관성, 서버리스 등 지난 20년간 클라우드 아키텍처를 형성한 핵심 개념과 교훈을 돌아봅니다.
abstract: Instant, vast scale and elasticity. Infrastructure as Code. Eventual consistency. Immutable infrastructure. Serverless. Event-driven computing. Internet of Things. Chaos engineering. Zero trust. Pervasive observability. Twenty years of cloud have produced an extraordinary density of patterns — each arriving with conviction and shaping what came next. Some became invisible foundations we build on without thinking. Others evolved in ways nobody predicted. And the evolution continues — now with agentic architectures. What has stood the test of time? What's still evolving? And what can we learn to be ready for the next twenty years?
